title: Staged Experiments SDK: canonical APIs for canary/A-B/shadowing and auto-revert
creator: Daniel Kim
description:
Problem: product and infra teams need a single, predictable API and SDK surface for running staged model experiments (canary rollouts, A/B tests, synthetic/shadow traffic) and for automatic reversion when quality or reliability regressions are detected. Current ad-hoc approaches lead to repeated build effort across clients and fragile manual rollbacks.

Goal: design an idempotent, permissioned, and observable rollout management API plus lightweight client helpers that: (1) let engineers create and update rollout configurations programmatically, (2) support traffic split semantics for canary and A/B experiments, (3) support silent shadowing for behavioral testing, (4) expose an auto-rollback policy engine driven by SLO/quality thresholds, and (5) avoid duplicate side effects via creation idempotency tokens and strong audit logs.

Scope: API surface for rollout CRUD and actions, SDK client helpers (Python/Node), backend contract for idempotency and model variant compatibility checks, RBAC mappings, telemetry contract for rollout events and metrics, rollout lifecycle states and permitted transitions, and docs/examples for typical migration patterns. Not in scope: UI console polish (separate ticket) and advanced ML evaluation logic (we rely on existing evals infra).
acceptance_criteria: API endpoints exist for creating, listing, retrieving, updating, and performing actions on rollouts (create/update must be idempotent)
SDK helpers for Python and Node provide a small surface: create_rollout(...), update_traffic(...), promote(), rollback(), shadow_test()
Permission model enforces separate scopes for rollout-management and traffic-override; audit logs capture actor and idempotency token
Auto-rollback policy supports time-windowed error-rate and eval-regression thresholds and can be toggled per rollout
Telemetry emitted to metrics/logging with documented metric names and tags for tracing rollouts across services
Integration tests cover idempotency (duplicate create requests) and a simulated auto-rollback scenario
updates: 2026-02-11: Kickoff with Eng (Liam O'Connor) and Security (Aisha Patel). Agreed to require idempotency token and return 409 only for conflicting immutable fields.

2026-02-18: Chose API verbs and routes. Drafted POST /v1/rollouts with idempotency-key header; PATCH for traffic changes. Decision: traffic updates are additive and must include expected_version for optimistic concurrency.
2026-02-25: Design review with SDK leads. Decided lightweight helpers instead of heavy client state machines; helpers will accept rollout config and return rollout object with status and events URL.

2026-03-04: Security review kickoff. Recommended split scopes: rollout.create, rollout.modify, rollout.override_traffic, rollout.rollback. Added audit log requirement and KMS key for signed rollout manifests.

2026-03-10: Eng spike implemented idempotency store using consistent hashing of (owner, idempotency-key). Found race when two creates arrive with same key but differing payloads — agreed to return 409 and record both payloads in audit for investigating clients.
2026-03-12: Integration test added in platform CI to simulate auto-rollback when error_rate > 2% over 5m window. Test currently flakes in the simulator; Eng investigating timing assumptions.
comments: Liam O'Connor (ENG): For traffic split semantics we recommend expressing splits as explicit percentages with a fallback mapping to compatible model variants. Need a compatibility matrix check before allowing a rollout to reach >0% traffic.

Aisha Patel (SECURITY): Audit trail must include idempotency-key and resolving actor. Also require that the rollout manifest is signed by the requester's service account using KMS for high-privilege rollouts (traffic >50% or cross-tenant).

Maya Singh (DX): SDK surface should prioritize async helpers returning a handle that streams events; developers want live progress updates during canary ramp-ups. We'll prototype a 'wait_for_stable' helper.

Sofia Martinez (PM, assignee): Action items - (1) finalize API contract by 2026-03-18, (2) land SDK prototypes and docs for examples, (3) add two integration tests for idempotency and auto-rollback flakiness.

Code review feedback (PR #2157): reviewer suggested making traffic updates idempotent as well by allowing client to provide an expected_traffic_version token; we adopted optimistic concurrency instead of server-side locks to reduce latency.
implementation_notes: API: POST /v1/rollouts - body: rollout_config, headers: Idempotency-Key, X-Requested-By. Returns rollout_id and status. Duplicate create with same Idempotency-Key returns same rollout object if payloads match; otherwise 409 + recorded payloads.

API: PATCH /v1/rollouts/{id}/traffic - body: {splits:[{variant,percent}]}, header: If-Match: rollout-version. Server validates compatibility and rejects if sum != 100 for production rollouts or if percent pushes canary above configured max without explicit approval.

Actions: POST /v1/rollouts/{id}/actions/promote and /actions/rollback. Promote is a convenience to advance a canary to 100% using a controlled ramp policy. Rollback accepts reason and optional snapshot id.

Shadowing: POST /v1/rollouts/{id}/shadow - creates a shadowing route that duplicates live requests to the target model without affecting response path. Shadow routes are limited to non-sensitive customer data unless data-masking is enabled.

Auto-rollback: configurable policy on rollout (thresholds, window, evaluation metric). Policy engine emits events rollout.policy.evaluated and rollout.policy.action with tags {rollout_id, metric, window} that the Console will consume to surface automated reverts.

Telemetry contract: metrics prefix 'rollout.' with counters and histograms: rollout.requests, rollout.errors, rollout.latency_ms, rollout.traffic_percent, rollout.rollback_count. Logs must correlate with request_id and rollout_id.

Permissions: map to RBAC scopes; higher-impact actions (traffic_override, manual_rollback) restricted to elevated roles. Implementation will reuse existing authz middleware with a new resource type 'rollout'.

SDK: Python and Node helpers will accept semantic config objects and idempotency_key arg. Helpers will expose async iterator for events and an abort token for cancelling ramps. Examples to include canary-ramp and A/B-compare notebooks.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Misconfigured auto-rollback could flip-flop rolls under noisy telemetry. Mitigation: require hysteresis (cooldown windows) and require minimum sample counts before evaluation.
Risk: Duplicate creation attempts by retrying clients could silently diverge. Mitigation: idempotency-key semantics + audit trail + clear 409 behavior for conflicting payloads.
Risk: Shadowing leaks PII. Mitigation: default shadowing to redacted payloads and require opt-in for sensitive data with audit justification.
Risk: Permission scope explosion. Mitigation: keep a small, composable scope set and provide Console roles that map to scope bundles for common personas.
